facts.raw_span: involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs for more than 10 days
a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
slow response, reduced muscle strength, and positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs
Continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude were observed in the left arm and leg
a blood glucose level of 8.59 mmol/L
a hemoglobin A1c of 7.43%
all other laboratory values within normal limits
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
without evidence of acute infarction
high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

concepts.why: The patient's involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs, described as continuous and irregular with variable amplitude, are characteristic of hemichorea.

The combination of the patient's untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus, elevated blood glucose and hemoglobin A1c levels, and the imaging findings of increased density in the bilateral striatal regions and high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia, suggest a diagnosis of diabetic striatal disease.
The imaging findings of increased density in the bilateral striatal regions and high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia indicate basal ganglia disease.
The patient's elevated blood glucose and hemoglobin A1c levels, in combination with the involuntary movements, suggest a hyperglycemia-related movement disorder.

The patient's slow response, reduced muscle strength, and positive tendon reflexes, along with the imaging findings, could suggest vascular parkinsonism, although the absence of acute infarction makes this less likely.
